sources.title: A Climate Landscape Analysis for Children: Policy Brief
sources.temporal_coverage: Child climate and environmental vulnerability synthesis, including observed events and health reports through 2023.
sources.methodology: Four-page UNICEF policy brief summarizing its 2024 Climate Landscape Analysis for Children.
sources.limitations: Brief-level summary; it gives no district rates or causal estimates.

sources.title: Mine Action and the Resilience of Communities to Climate Change
sources.organization: Geneva International Centre for Humanitarian Demining (GICHD)
sources.temporal_coverage: Mine-action policy and community case studies, including clearance activity through 2023 and status statements made in the report.
sources.methodology: Document review and interviews; Kosovo material covers mine-action institutions and two local cases.
sources.limitations: Qualitative cases are not causal impact evaluations; status reflects the report period.

sources.title: Intervention Plan for Rural Development to Mitigate and Adapt to Climate Change, 2023–2028
sources.organization: Municipality of Prizren, with support from UNDP Kosovo
sources.temporal_coverage: Municipal rural-development plan for 2023–2028, dated November 2022.
sources.methodology: Municipal sectoral intervention plan with proposed actions, timelines, responsible offices and estimated costs.
sources.limitations: The plan records proposals and scheduled actions, not verified implementation; 2023–2025 milestones are now elapsed.

sources.title: Community Flood Vulnerability and Adaptive Capacity in the Municipality of Podujeva: Results of the CLIPP Household Survey
sources.organization: University of Prishtina and Municipality of Podujeva
sources.temporal_coverage: Household survey conducted 1 June–31 July 2026; record version published 5 August 2026.
sources.methodology: Municipal household survey with 101 responses; the publisher record summarizes aggregated findings and methods.
sources.limitations: Publisher record only was accessible; findings describe participating households, not a representative municipal sample; item denominators vary.

claims.paraphrase: The brief names Ferizaj and Prizren as most vulnerable; children facing both hazard exposure and multidimensional poverty face greatest risks.
claims.limitations: No district rates or causal estimates are provided.

claims.paraphrase: After 2021 and 2023 were Kosovo's hottest years, family medicine centres in Pristina and Mitrovica reported more child admissions, especially above 30°C.
claims.limitations: No admission counts or attribution analysis are supplied.

claims.locator: PDF p. 2, ‘Heavy Rainfall and Flooding’ section.
claims.paraphrase: Early-2023 floods affected about 22,000 people, including 3,000 children, mostly in Skenderaj and Mitrovica. Average-year floods affect about 10,000 people, damaging homes/schools and interrupting water and power.
claims.limitations: The annual estimate is national; affected people are not all children.

claims.locator: PDF pp. 1–2, vulnerability summary and ‘Wildfires’ section.
claims.paraphrase: UNICEF flags disabled/health-condition and Roma, Ashkali and Egyptian children as facing added challenges; fires increased since 2007 in Mitrovica and Prizren, while human-caused fires removed 13% of Kosovo tree cover in 2001–2023.
claims.limitations: Fires are not attributed to climate change; tree-cover loss is countrywide.

claims.locator: Printed p. 39, Kosovo mine-action priority-setting discussion.
claims.paraphrase: KMAC weighs risk, environment/development and poverty in site priorities; hazards contributing to climate impacts receive top clearance priority. Operators lacked climate-specific procedures at report time.
affected_groups: communities using farmland, grazing land and forests
claims.limitations: Reported criteria/status, not clearance outcomes or current operating rules.

claims.locator: Printed p. 40, case study 1, Bjeshkët e Nemuna National Park.
claims.paraphrase: War ordnance contaminated wooded hills west of Peja, which faces flash floods, hotter summers and milder, less snowy winters. Clearance released 355,502 m², reopening park trails and resource access.
claims.limitations: Qualitative case; no measured climate outcome.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Report says ordnance restricted park access; clearance restored it and supported long-term climate resilience.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 41–42, case study 2, Barë and Bajgora villages.
claims.paraphrase: In Mitrovica, war/industrial-closure migration and weakened services coexist with hotter summers, less snow and possible July–August drought. Clearance restored Barë grazing/firewood access and Bajgora woodland/pipeline access; wind power was exported.
claims.limitations: Qualitative case; drought is potential and resilience benefits incidental.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Report links postwar/industrial-closure economic challenges to migration and weaker services; clearance restored livelihood/resource access.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 5–6, executive summary and intervention plan summary table.
claims.paraphrase: Prizren's 2023–2028 rural plan sets out 14 measures and 74 proposed actions with estimated costs of €22.4955 million across agriculture, biodiversity, forestry and rural tourism.
claims.limitations: Budget and actions are planned, not confirmed expenditure or delivered outputs; some plan milestones have elapsed.

claims.paraphrase: The plan proposed irrigation-system rehabilitation studies, water-storage studies, Manastrica Dam design/construction for drinking water and irrigation, drip-irrigation subsidies and ponds for irrigation/firefighting; dam construction was scheduled for 2025–2028.
institutions: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Rural Development
claims.limitations: These are commitments in a 2022 plan; the record does not verify construction or completed studies.

claims.paraphrase: The plan flags women in rural Prizren as potentially responsible for agricultural water management yet having limited water access; it calls for women's participation in planning, early warnings and drought-tolerant seed support.
claims.limitations: The plan identifies gender considerations and proposed measures; it supplies no local prevalence estimate or outcome assessment.

claims.paraphrase: A June–July 2026 Podujeva survey of 101 respondents across 35 settlements found recurrent, materially damaging floods among participating households, with impacts concentrated on agricultural land and crops.
claims.limitations: The survey is indicative of participating households, not statistically representative of Podujeva; report PDF was inaccessible.

claims.paraphrase: The Podujeva record reports widespread drinking-water interruptions, limited private drainage, infrequent channel cleaning, low uptake of protective measures and warnings reaching roughly two-thirds of respondents.
claims.limitations: Percentages use item-level valid responses with varying denominators; the survey is non-representative and the report file was inaccessible.

access_audit.locator: Complete four-page policy brief, especially pp. 1–2.
access_audit.notes: Publisher PDF was opened and cited passages read directly; this is a brief summarizing a larger assessment.

access_audit.locator: Complete 79-page report; Kosovo overview and case studies, printed pp. 38–42.
access_audit.notes: Full publisher PDF read directly. Local cases are qualitative accounts and the institutional status is vintage-bound.

access_audit.locator: Complete 32-page municipal plan; printed pp. 5–6, 11 and 15–16.
access_audit.notes: Full plan read directly; interventions are proposed actions, not verified results.

access_audit.locator: Publisher record ‘Description’ and ‘Methods (English)’ sections; linked report file not read.
access_audit.notes: Zenodo record provides the author/municipal description and survey-method summary. Direct report download returned HTTP 429; no indexed snippets used.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Record does not state a license; unknown.

search_audit.query: Kosovo district, municipality and settlement climate vulnerability children flood heat wildfire local climate report
search_audit.outcome: Directly read UNICEF's Kosovo child-climate brief and Prizren's municipal rural intervention plan; a 2026 Podujeva household survey was usable only through its publisher summary.

search_audit.query: Kosovo climate change conflict social tension natural resources local evidence mine contamination displacement
search_audit.outcome: No directly read source established a climate-triggered violent-conflict event or tested climate-to-conflict mediation. GICHD documents a reverse pathway: conflict-related ordnance restricted land/resource access; clearance supported local resilience.

search_audit.query: Kosovo war legacy explosive ordnance climate adaptation water forestry mine action institutional constraints
search_audit.outcome: GICHD's directly read Kosovo programme review identifies ordnance-contaminated land/resource access, municipal consultation, and dated gaps in operator climate procedures; it does not show climate effects causing conflict.

search_audit.query: Kosovo local resilience adaptation plans flood warning water access mine clearance community capacity
search_audit.outcome: Read the Prizren plan's proposed irrigation and water-storage actions, GICHD's Peja/Mitrovica land-release cases, and Podujeva survey summary; plan milestones and household-survey representativeness remain limitations.

gaps: The Podujeva report PDF returned HTTP 429; findings are limited to the University of Prishtina/Municipality publisher record's explicit methods and results summary.
No directly inspected evidence established a climate-triggered violent-conflict event or a local climate-to-conflict causal estimate; this is an evidence gap, not evidence of absence.
Prizren plan actions and budgets are commitments, and several earlier milestones elapsed; implementation status was not checked.
GICHD's conflict-related land-access and resilience evidence is qualitative and report-period-specific; it does not quantify adaptation impacts.
